scope: Adaptive repeated development on the fixed 4977-center Okutama cohort; this standalone evidence screen does not train a fusion with ARFTR.
research_question: Can jointly observed, timestamped actor-frame descriptors improve state recognition, and does actor-relative representation plus action-change supervision improve over a matched ordinary temporal encoder?

inputs.frame_features: Frozen DINOv2 base CLS descriptors at the 16 short and 16 long exact actor-frame timestamps.
inputs.frame_targets: Known action target at each valid cached physical actor frame; supervision is restricted to current outer-training scenarios.

architecture.actor_relative: projected frame state plus its difference from the masked local actor mean
architecture.relation: same-versus-different action state for valid, distinct timestamp pairs inside training sequences only

training.class_loss: outer-training center class weights plus physical-frame multiplicity weights for frame and pair supervision
training.selection: none; architecture, optimizer, relation weight and resource budget are fixed before fitting
training.outer_metric_embargo: Held labels are not read by an individual fit; predictions release only after the complete 75-fit inventory.

stop_rules.no_sequence_arm_improves_arfter: stop cached global-descriptor sequence integration and move to a new observation type
stop_rules.ordinary_tcn_beats_actor_relative: retain ordinary temporal evidence and reject the actor-relative mechanism
stop_rules.primary_passes: rebuild full inner-nested candidate and ARFTR predictions before any fusion or utility analysis
